title: Set 266

sentences.ko: 윗집에 어린 남자애가 하나 있는데, 아침 여섯 시쯤부터 집 이쪽 끝에서 저쪽 끝까지 뛰어다녀. 올라가서 한마디 해야 하나 계속 생각은 하는데, 대체 뭐라고 해? 애한테 걷지 말라고 하라고?
sentences.text: The family upstairs has a little boy who runs from one end of the apartment to the other starting at like six in the morning. I keep thinking I should go up and say something, but what am I supposed to say, tell your kid to stop walking?

alts.text: Upstairs there's this little kid who runs back and forth across their whole apartment from like six in the morning. I keep meaning to go up there and say something, but what do I even say, tell your kid to quit walking?

The family living above us has a young son who runs from one end of their apartment to the other, beginning at around six in the morning. I keep thinking that I ought to go upstairs and speak with them, but what exactly am I supposed to say? Should I ask them to tell their child to stop walking?

sentences.note: **I keep thinking I should** 는 ~해야 하나 계속 생각한다는 뜻이에요. **what am I supposed to say** 는 대체 뭐라고 하라는 거야, 할 말이 마땅치 않을 때 쓰는 말이에요.

sentences.ko: 그러니까 걔가 간호사인데 야간 근무를 해서 아직 싱글인 거야. 뭐 문제가 있어서 그런 게 아니고. 근데 말을 엄청 직설적으로 해서, 네가 재미없다 싶으면 금방 알게 될걸.
sentences.text: So she's a nurse and she works nights, which is why she's still single, not because there's anything wrong with her. She's really blunt, though, so if she thinks you're boring, you'll know pretty fast.

alts.text: Okay, she's a nurse, works nights, that's why she's still single. It's not like something's wrong with her. She's super blunt though, so if she thinks you're boring, you'll find out quick.

She is a nurse who works night shifts, which is the reason she is still single, not because there is anything wrong with her. She is very direct, however, so if she finds you boring, you will know rather quickly.

sentences.note: **blunt** 는 돌려 말하지 않고 직설적인 사람을 말해요. **which is why** 는 그래서 ~인 거다, 앞 말이 이유일 때 이어 붙여요.
sentences.situation: 친구 소개팅 주선하면서 상대가 어떤 사람인지 설명하기

sentences.ko: 그냥 걔한테 결혼식 일 아직도 서운하다고 말하고 싶은 마음도 있는데, 지금 그 얘길 꺼내면 일 년 내내 꽁해 있었던 것처럼 보일 거야. 뭐, 사실 좀 그렇긴 했지. 모르겠다, 너라면 어떻게 할 거야?
sentences.text: Part of me wants to just tell her I'm still upset about the wedding thing, but if I bring it up now, it's going to look like I've been holding a grudge for a year. Which, okay, I kind of have. I don't know, what would you do?

alts.text: I kinda wanna just tell her I'm still mad about the wedding thing, but if I bring it up now, it's gonna look like I've been holding a grudge for a year. Which, yeah, I sort of have. I dunno, what would you do?

Part of me would like to tell her that I am still upset about what happened at the wedding, but if I raise it now, it will appear that I have been holding a grudge for a year. Which, admittedly, I have. I am not sure. What would you do?

sentences.note: **holding a grudge** 는 앙금을 품고 있다, 뒤끝이 있다는 뜻이에요. **bring it up** 은 그 얘기를 꺼내다예요. **Part of me wants to** 는 ~하고 싶은 마음도 있다는 말이에요.
sentences.situation: 친구한테 고민 상담하면서 결론은 못 내리기

sentences.ko: 현장학습 이메일 받았어? 학부모가 차로 데려다줘야 한다는데, 그게 수요일 오전이래. 우리가 다 직장이 없는 줄 아나 봐.
sentences.text: Did you get that email about the field trip? They need parents to drive, but it's on a Wednesday morning, so I guess they think none of us have jobs.

alts.text: You see the field trip email? They want parent drivers on a Wednesday morning, like none of us work.
Did you receive the email regarding the field trip? They are asking for parents to drive, but it is on a Wednesday morning, so I suppose they assume that none of us are employed.

sentences.note: **field trip** 은 현장학습이에요. **I guess they think** 는 아마 ~라고 생각하나 보다, 살짝 비꼬는 말투로도 잘 써요.

sentences.ko: 이런 말 하기 미안한데, 베이비시터한테 열 시까지 간다고 했고 그 애가 내일 학교도 가야 해서 우리 슬슬 일어나야 할 것 같아. 그래도 진짜 재밌었어, 다음엔 우리 집에서 하자.
sentences.text: I hate to do this, but we told the babysitter we'd be back by ten, and she's got school tomorrow, so we should probably get going. This was really fun, though, let's do it at our place next time.

alts.text: Ugh, sorry, but we told the sitter we'd be home by ten and she's got school tomorrow, so we'd better head out. This was super fun though, next time's at our place.

I am sorry to do this, but we told the babysitter we would be back by ten, and she has school tomorrow, so we should probably be leaving. We truly enjoyed this, though. Next time, please come to our home.

sentences.note: **I hate to do this, but** 은 미안하지만 ~, 먼저 자리를 뜰 때 자주 꺼내는 말이에요. **get going** 은 슬슬 가 보다는 뜻이고, casual 의 **head out** 도 같은 뜻이에요.
sentences.situation: 저녁 모임에서 먼저 일어날 구실 만들기

reviewed: 4번 casual 이 text 와 앞부분이 거의 같아서(You see that email about the field trip? They need parents to drive) 더 짧고 축약된 구어로 새로 씀
